name: Bohemian style

image.caption: Young woman with short red hair and bohemian style in Madison, Wisconsin 2023

lead: Bohemian style, often called boho, is an unconventional fashion look built on loose, flowing clothing, natural fabrics, earthy colors, patterns and layered jewelry. It projects a relaxed, artistic, individual image.

It grows from the dress of 19th-century Parisian artists and recurred through the 1960s hippie era and the boho-chic wave of the early 2000s, when figures such as Kate Moss and Sienna Miller popularised it.

paras: People assemble it from peasant blouses, maxi skirts or dresses, wide-leg pants, suede boots, scarves, beaded jewelry and hats, often thrifted or vintage, layering textures and prints in earthy tones.
No health risks; it is a clothing style. Commentators note it borrows from Romani and other cultures, which some find sensitive.

lead: Bohemian style, or boho chic, is a fashion look characterised by flowing fabrics, natural woven materials, bright or earthy colors, layered jewelry and loose, unrestricted shapes [1]. People use it to present a relaxed, creative and individual appearance.

The word comes from French bohémien, a mistaken association of Romani people with Bohemia, and was applied to artists and writers in Paris's Latin Quarter in the 1840s [2][3]. Henri Murger's stories of bohemian life helped spread the image [2].
The look returned repeatedly: the 1960s hippie fashion, 1970s peasant dresses, and the early-2000s boho-chic of Kate Moss and Sienna Miller [1].
infobox: Maxi dresses, peasant blouses, fringe, scarves

paras: Core elements include flowing fabrics and natural weaves, full skirts, layered jewelry, flowers in the hair, and loose dress that rejects corseting [1]. Palettes tend toward earthy hues with paisley, floral and embroidered patterns [3].

In the 1840s, young artists in Paris's Latin Quarter were associated with poverty, devotion to art and disdain for money, an image romanticised by Murger and later by Puccini's La boheme [2]. The 1860s Pre-Raphaelite circle shaped dress, the 1920s brought bobs and shorter hems, and 1950s Left Bank bohemians wore mostly black [1]. The Beatles' Hamburg period, Swinging London and the 1967 Summer of Love brought hippie fashion mainstream [1]. In the early 2000s, Kate Moss and Sienna Miller popularised boho chic [1].

Writers on the style note that the term's roots lie in a mistaken label for Romani people and that the 19th-century look was an artistic pose by largely middle-class creators [3]. Critics cited by one source observe that commercial boho-chic diluted the original anti-materialist ethos [3].
